A Reader Asks His Congressman About Will Foster
Who Will Be In Prison Four Times Longer Than Rapists
The Local Media Doesn’t Care -- What One Person Can Do

(Marijuananews note: This letter offers an excellent example of what one person can do.)

From a reader:

August 18, 1999

Constituent of J. C. Watts demands Watts' Attention to Plight of Will Foster

Lawton, OK----

The liveliest topic today in Congressman J C Watts' town meeting was about Will Foster, a Oklahoman who was sentenced to 93 years in prison for growing his own medical marijuana.

Congressman Watts did not know that Will Foster was at the time and still is in the new private prison just opened in Lawton, Oklahoma, a scant ten miles from the town meeting site, in Watts' district.

While dancing around the main question as to whether the egregious sentence was moral or appropriate, given that in this same week in Oklahoma rapists are up for parole after 5 years in the pen, Watts did say that he would check into Will's medical status.

That would be a good thing, since Will is denied his medicine of choice... Marijuana. That point was made quite handily today.

Will's original sentence was reduced to 20 years, but that is twenty years too much for his ‘crime.' Couple that with the lack of proper medical care and you get a hardship sentence not justified for anyone in this "Land of the Free."

The constituent plans to follow up and assure that Watts' office does look into Will's predicament. More information will be provided as things happen.

You can guess how many of the 6 media reps asked me anything more after the meeting ... zero.
